Please see the link below.https://insolvencynotices.asic.gov.au/browsesearch-notices/notice-details/P-and-N-PTY-LTD-130845199/14e93daf-a8ba-4bcf-8428-ed7e39181b51Presently, we are new company and new management and provide online support to old customer on free of cost. Rest of the services is chargeable.  As your concern is for solar panel.  You have installed APS Poly panel., It is no longer available in market and it is also not a CEC approved brand.Hence it is difficult to claim warranty on you solar panel."This response was baffling as, when, on 15 November 2018 I expressed concern in relation to ASIC's insolvency notice via phone, and asked whether Euro Solar had gone into liquidation, they said "no", and words to the effect of "there was a problem with old management, but new management there is no problem, I can get boss to send you an e-mail about that if you like?â€  I was unconvinced, so, in response, I read the ASIC Liquidation Notice (which I was looking at at the time) and again expressed concern about the company winding up before my other warranty problem was resolved, leaving me to replace it at my own cost.  Harik assured me no such thing would happen.I immediately file noted that conversation, hence I am able to recall it in such a great amount of detail.In response to the e-mail of 6 February 2019 concerning my 'low voltage issue', I asked whether the manufacturer of my solar panels could be contacted with a view to resolving the issue under warranty.The e-mail response (also sent on 6 February 2019) was "Manufacturer has wind up their operation in Australia.  Sorry for the trouble to you."
